title: Checking your face in a new situation is listed at 2 years
summary: Most children look at a caregiver's face to see how to react in a new situation by about 2 years, CDC says.
body: CDC's 2-year social list includes looking at your face to see how to react in a new situation. The glance borrows another person's reaction when the place is unfamiliar. Most means 75 percent or more on that page. It is not a claim that a child must stare, and a research review argues that eye contact is not the only sign of engagement across cultures. The CDC materials are not a screening test. The age is the US checklist's age.
